newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close up on dollar, polls.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close up on dollar, polls.

text.p: French stocks finished higher on Monday, bolstered by polls showing the ruling coalition set to win an upcoming parliamentary election and a stronger dollar.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 13.99 points, or 0.55 percent, at 2,550.25, while the CAC-40 April futures contract rose 17 points to 2,562.
Volume was a relatively light 3.4 billion francs, with many investors feeling cautious ahead of a slew of U.S. economic indicators due out later in the week.
Four polls published since Sunday put the conservatives ahead and Sofres and IFOP polls gave them a wide lead.

* Shares in retailer Casino closed up 3.11 percent at 265.50 francs on merger talk rekindled by the chairman's remarks in a newspaper interview that it was important to build a second French food retailer with annual sales of around 200 billion francs, in addition to leader Carrefour.
Asked about a possible and much-rumoured linkup between Casino and Promodes, Casino chairman Georges Plassat told the newspaper Les Echos that anything was possible.
* Bouygues shares rose 2.11 percent to 532 francs. The group told a news conference it had retained Societe Generale to help find a buyer for its Ciby 2000 film unit.
* Insurer GAN, which closed down 1.56 percent to 151 francs, is expected to report a 1996 loss of around five billion francs this evening.
* Alcatel Alsthom fell 1.74 percent to 623 francs. Traders cited German press reports of an antitrust probe into electric cable manufacturers, including two subsidiaries of Alcatel SEL.
* U.S. economic data due this week include U.S. durable goods orders, GDP, spending, cars, jobs and NAPM index.
